
tidydiversity brings biodiversity estimation into the tidyverse. Every
function takes a long data frame, with one row per site and species, and
returns a tibble you can filter, join and plot with the tools you already
use.

```{r setup}
library(tidydiversity)
library(dplyr)
```

## The example data

tidydiversity ships with real field data from Papua New Guinea. The main
example, `png_ants`, records ground-foraging ants at nutrient baits along
the Mt Wilhelm elevational gradient, from 200 to 3700 m, in the dry and the
wet season (Moses et al. 2023, *Global Ecology and Biogeography*). Each row
is one ant species at one bait.

```{r}
png_ants
```

Ants recruit to baits, so worker counts measure activity rather than
independent individuals. `png_ants` therefore has no `abundance` column:
tidydiversity counts each row once, and diversity is estimated from the
number of baits at which each species was found.

Three more Papua New Guinea datasets cover other designs and taxa:

* `png_tree_ants`: every ant nest in 1254 trees in plots at 200, 900 and
  1800 m (Plowman et al. 2020).
* `png_frogs`: 3390 frogs of 55 species at eight elevations on Mt Wilhelm
  (Dahl et al. 2023).
* `wanang_butterflies`: butterflies counted on 36 days over three years in
  the Wanang forest dynamics plot (Luk et al. 2019).

## Tidy the community

`as_community()` sums repeated records, drops zeros and gives standard
column names. Use your own column names through the `site`, `species` and
`abundance` arguments.

```{r}
ants <- as_community(png_ants, .by = season)
ants
```

If your data arrive as a site by species matrix, `community_long()` turns
it into long format, and `community_wide()` goes the other way.

```{r}
wide <- community_wide(ants, .by = season)
wide[, 1:6]
```

## Grouping

All verbs accept `.by`, and they respect `group_by()`:

```{r}
png_ants |>
  group_by(season) |>
  div_hill(q = 0) |>
  arrange(desc(diversity))
```
